The '''2019–20 Premier League''' was the 28th season of the [[Premier League]], the top English professional [[association football|football]] league, since its establishment in 1992, and the 121st season of top-flight English football overall. The season started on 9 August 2019 and concluded on 26 July 2020.<ref name="auto"/> [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] were the defending champions for the second successive year, after picking up the [[Treble (association football)|domestic treble]] the previous season.

The season was halted for over three months, following a decision on 13 March 2020 by the Premier League to suspend the league after a number of players and other club staff became ill due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The initial suspension, until 4 April, was then extended to mid-June.<ref name="05Apr" /> The season recommenced with two matches on 17 June and a full round of matches played over the weekend of 19–22 June.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League returns on June 17|work=Sky Sports|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11996065/premier-league-returns-on-june-17|access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref>

[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] were crowned champions for the first time since [[1989–90 Football League First Division|1990]]. Their title win was also the club's first of the Premier League era and nineteenth overall. Over the season, the club set a number of [[Football records and statistics in England|English top-flight records]] including the earliest title win (with seven games to spare),<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mendola|first=Nicholas|date=25 June 2020|title=Earliest Premier League champion: Is Liverpool fastest to clinch?|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/earliest-premier-league-title-winners-in-history|access-date=2020-06-25|website=ProSoccerTalk {{!}} NBC Sports|language=en-US}}</ref> the latest title win (securing the title on 25 June),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.squawka.com/en/jurgen-klopp-liverpool-records-premier-league-title/|title=Liverpool 2019/20 stats: Major Premier League records the Reds could break this season}}</ref> the biggest points lead at any time (25),<ref name=PMrecords>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1561869 |title=Which Premier League records have Liverpool set? |website=Premier League |date=5 January 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> and the most consecutive home wins (24, of which 7 were carried over from the previous season).<ref name=PMrecords/>

The season introduced the controversial [[video assistant referee]] (VAR) review system.<ref>{{cite news |title=VAR: Video assistant referees set to be used in Premier League next season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46224473 |access-date=7 April 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 November 2018}}</ref> Changes to the laws affecting backpasses, penalties, handballs and substitutions were also introduced in 2019–20.<ref>{{cite news |title=Football's new laws – changes to backpasses, penalties, handballs and subs for 2019–20 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48965849 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=2 August 2019 |date=1 August 2019}}</ref>

== Summary ==
The Premier League season marked the start of a new three-year TV deal. One key change was that eight matches were shown on television at 19:45 on Saturdays across the season, broadcast by [[Sky Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|date=12 June 2019|title=Premier League broadcast deals for 2019–2022|website=premierleague.com|publisher=Premier League|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/970151|access-date=23 April 2020}}</ref> Further, [[Amazon Prime Video|Amazon]] broadcast two rounds of fixtures in December, including the [[Merseyside derby]], marking the first time an entire round of live matches had been broadcast domestically.<ref>{{Cite news|date=13 June 2019|title=Record 200 Premier League matches to be shown live next season|work=[[The Times]]|url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/technology/article/record-200-premier-league-matches-to-be-shown-live-next-season-b9gxns5d0|access-date=15 June 2019|quote=Of the 380 games across the season, 200 will be broadcast live and particular interest will be paid to the two full rounds of matches in December that will be screened by Amazon at the start of its first three-year deal.}}</ref>

It was the first Premier League season to have a mid-season break in February. Three games of a normal round of ten were played on the weekend 8–9 February 2020, six games on the following weekend 14–17 February and the tenth game, Manchester City versus [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], was rescheduled from 9 February to 19 February due to [[Storm Ciara]]. Games played on the same day had separate time slots such that the games did not overlap.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelner |first1=Martha |date=8 June 2018 |title=Premier League winter break to come into force in 2019–20 season |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/08/winter-break-to-come-into-force-in-premier-league-england |access-date=7 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Callaghan |first=Rory |date=June 8, 2018 |title=Premier League winter break approved from 2019-20, FA confirms |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11398471/premier-league-winter-break-approved-from-2019-20-fa-confirms |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=[[Sky Sports]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City v West Ham set for 19 February |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51467120 |access-date=2024-01-07 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tanner |first=Joe |date=February 11, 2020 |title=Man City vs West Ham rearranged for February 19 and live on Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11931538/man-city-vs-west-ham-rearranged-for-february-19-and-live-on-sky-sports |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Robson |first=Jack Rosser, James |date=2020-02-11 |title=Man City vs West Ham rescheduled for Wednesday February 19 |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/manchester-city-west-ham-rearranged-premier-league-next-week-a4359046.html |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=Evening Standard |language=en}}</ref>

=== Title race ===
With Manchester City and Liverpool achieving 98 and 97 points respectively in the [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19 season]], many expected another close race for the title. Liverpool led the 2019-20 Premier League for almost all of the season, eventually finishing as champions and marking their first league title in 30 years and their first of the Premier League era after Manchester City lost 2-1 to [[Chelsea F.C|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 25 June 2020.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 June 2020 |title=Chelsea 2 Man City 1 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51884262 |access-date=29 June 2020 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Upon winning the league, Liverpool claimed the unusual [[Premier League records and statistics#Titles|achievement]] of winning the Premier League earlier than any other team by games played (with seven games remaining) and later than any other team by date (the only team to clinch the title in the month of June).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendola |first=Nicholas |date=25 June 2020 |title=Earliest Premier League champion: Is Liverpool fastest to clinch? |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/earliest-premier-league-title-winners-in-history |access-date=25 June 2020 |work=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Records and achievements ===
On 25 October 2019, [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] broke the Premier League record – as well as the all-time English top-flight record – for the largest away league win and equalled the biggest ever Premier League win when they defeated [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] [[Southampton F.C. 0–9 Leicester City F.C.|9–0]] at [[St Mary's Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|date=25 October 2019|title=Southampton 0–9 Leicester City: Foxes equal record for biggest Premier League win|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50092694|access-date=25 October 2019}}</ref>

During the season, Liverpool broke or tied several [[Premier League records and statistics|Premier League all-time records]]. They achieved a record-equalling 18 consecutive wins<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ouzia |first=Malik |date=24 February 2020 |title=Liverpool equal Premier League winning run record with victory over West Ham |work=Evening Standard |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/liverpool-equal-premier-league-winning-run-record-a4370351.html |access-date=24 February 2020}}</ref> before being defeated by [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on 29 February. They also set records of 24 consecutive home wins,<ref name="PMrecords" /> and a 25-point lead in the table at any time.<ref name="PMrecords" />

On 12 January 2020, in a 6–1 victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], Manchester City's [[Sergio Agüero]] broke [[Thierry Henry]]'s Premier League record for most goals scored by an overseas player.<ref>{{cite news|date=13 January 2020|title=Sergio Aguero overtakes Thierry Henry to become Premier League record overseas goalscorer|work=Sky Sports|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11679/11907092/sergio-aguero-overtakes-thierry-henry-to-become-premier-league-record-overseas-goalscorer|access-date=13 January 2020}}</ref> In the same match, he also broke the record for most hat-tricks scored by a single player (12), previously held by [[Alan Shearer]].<ref>{{cite news|date=12 January 2020|title=Man City star Sergio Aguero sets Premier League hat-tricks record|work=talkSPORT|url=https://talksport.com/football/654620/man-city-sergio-aguero-records-premier-league-hat-tricks|access-date=13 January 2020}}</ref>

=== Black Lives Matter impact ===
As a gesture of solidarity following the [[murder of George Floyd]], players' names on the back of their shirts were replaced with '[[Black Lives Matter]]' for the first 12 matches of the restarted season as well as replacing the Premier League badge for the BLM's for the rest of the season. The Premier League also gave their support for any player who chooses to "[[U.S. national anthem protests (2016–present)|take a knee]]" before or during matches.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 June 2020|title=Premier League players to wear 'Black Lives Matter' on back of shirts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53030146|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> In addition, the [[National Health Service (England)|NHS]] tribute badge was also used at all kits for the remainder of the season.

=== Relegation battle ===
On 11 July 2020, Norwich City became the first team to be relegated to the [[2020–21 EFL Championship|Championship]] after a 4–0 defeat at home to West Ham United with three games remaining.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53283313|title = Norwich City 0-4 West Ham United|date=11 July 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=11 July 2020}}</ref> On 26 July 2020, the final day of the season, [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] were the second team to be relegated to the Championship, despite winning 3–1 away to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53460590|title = Everton 1-3 Bournemouth|date=26 July 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> Watford were the final team to be relegated to the Championship on the same day, after losing 3–2 away to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53460584|title = Arsenal 3-2 Watford|date=26 July 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref><!--Bournemouth were relegated before Watford, as the final whistle went at West Ham Vs. Aston Villa before Arsenal Vs. Watford-->  Both of these results were coupled with Aston Villa's 1–1 draw against West Ham United, ensuring Aston Villa safety in the Premier League for another season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53460591|title = West Ham United 1-1 Aston Villa|date=26 July 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> Coincidentally, the three relegated teams were the same teams promoted to the Premier League for the [[2015–16 Premier League|2015–16 season]].

==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic==
From March 2020, the season was affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/51859553|title=Coronavirus: UK government considering banning sporting fixtures|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020}}</ref> On 10 March, the match between Manchester City and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], due to be played the next day after being rescheduled due to City's participation in the [[2020 EFL Cup final]], was postponed. A number of Arsenal players had made close contact with [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] owner [[Evangelos Marinakis]], who had tested positive for infection with the [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|coronavirus]], when the two teams had met in the Europa League 13 days earlier.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester City vs. Arsenal postponed after players exposed to Olympiakos owner Evangelos Marinakis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-premier-league/story/4071980/arsenal-vs-manchester-city-postponed-after-players-exposed-to-olympiakos-owner-evangelos-marinakis |website=ESPN |access-date=10 March 2020 }}</ref> It was the first football season in England to be halted since the [[1939–40 in English football|1939–40 season]] was abandoned after only three games following the outbreak of the [[World War II|Second World War]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1939-40.html|title=Football Statistics Archive|website=RSSSF.com}}</ref>

On 12 March, it was revealed that three Leicester City players were self-isolating.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51856906| title=Coronavirus: Three Leicester City players in isolation after showing symptoms |work=BBC Sport |date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Manchester City announced that their defender [[Benjamin Mendy]] was also self-isolating, after a family member displayed symptoms of the virus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51864868|title=Benjamin Mendy: Man City player self-isolating, family member in hospital|work=BBC Sport|date=12 March 2020}}</ref> Later in the evening, it was then confirmed that Arsenal head coach [[Mikel Arteta]] had tested positive for coronavirus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51865442|title=Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager tests positive for coronavirus|work=BBC Sport|date=13 March 2020}}</ref> As a result of Arteta's positive test, the match between [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] and Arsenal, scheduled for 14 March at the [[Falmer Stadium|Amex]], was postponed.<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Brighton & Hove Albion FC |author-link=Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. |user=OfficialBHAFC |number=1238244369527984129 |date=12 March 2020 |title=Saturday's @premierleague match against @Arsenal has been postponed following the news that broke earlier this evening concerning Gunners head coach Mikel Arteta. #BHAFC |access-date=1 June 2020 }}</ref> On 13 March, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] announced that their winger [[Callum Hudson-Odoi]] had tested positive for coronavirus.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2020/03/13/chelsea-fc-training-facility-will-undergo-partial-closure-after-|title=Chelsea FC training facility will undergo partial closure after men's team player tested positive for COVID-19|website=chelseafc.com |publisher=Chelsea FC}}</ref>

On 13 March, following an emergency meeting between the Premier League, [[The Football Association]] (FA), the [[English Football League]] and the [[FA Women's Super League]], it was unanimously decided to suspend professional football in England until at least 4 April 2020.<ref name="Suspended">{{Cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1645173|title=Premier League, FA, EFL and WSL unite to postpone fixtures|date=13 March 2020|work=Premier League|access-date=13 March 2020}}</ref> On 19 March, the suspension was extended to at least 30 April 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51962751|title=Coronavirus: English football suspension extended until at least 30 April|work=BBC Sport|date=19 March 2020}}</ref> At the same time the FA agreed to extend the season indefinitely, past the scheduled end date of 1 June. In April 2020, the [[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care]], [[Matt Hancock]], called on Premier League players to take a pay cut during the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52142267|title=Coronavirus: Premier League players should take a pay cut – Matt Hancock|date=2 April 2020}}</ref> The [[Professional Footballers' Association|PFA]] rejected the call as they felt that a cut for all players would impact the [[Exchequer]] with a loss of income tax revenue.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pfa-statement-man-utd-city-18044468|title=PFA issues new statement on pay cut issues that affect Man Utd and City|first=Connor|last=O'Neill|date=4 April 2020|website=men}}</ref> Several clubs, including Watford, Southampton and West Ham United, all agreed to defer their wages.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52348498|title=Coronavirus and sport: Watford set to agree wage deferrals with players|date=19 April 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Even there was considered the option of cancelling the championship. Later in April, the Premier League produced a plan, nicknamed "Project Restart", aimed at restarting the league and playing all 92 remaining matches over a six-week period at approved, neutral stadiums.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/apr/29/premier-leagues-project-restart-what-is-it-and-is-it-feasible|title=Premier League's Project Restart: what is it and is it feasible?|first=Ed|last=Aarons|date=29 April 2020|work=The Guardian}}</ref> Watford, Aston Villa and Brighton, all near the bottom of the table, were of the opinion that it would be unfair to play the games in such different conditions when at risk of relegation but would be more in favour if the threat of relegation was removed.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52517532|title=Premier League: More clubs open to using neutral venues if relegation removed|date=3 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Watford oppose Premier League neutral venue proposals, joining Brighton and Aston Villa |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52598311 |website=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2020 |access-date=14 May 2020 }}</ref> From 19 May 2020, players were allowed to return to group training in preparation for restarting the league. They were permitted to be in groups of no more than five with all training sessions lasting no longer than 75 minutes for each player. [[Social distancing]] rules were required to be adhered to during the sessions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52704450|title=Project Restart: Premier League plan surprise inspections during training|date=18 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>
On 17 and 18 May, a total of 748 players and staff were tested for COVID-19. Six tests proved positive including [[Adrian Mariappa]] of Watford and Burnley assistant manager, [[Ian Woan]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1670563|title=Statement on results of COVID-19 tests|website=premierleague.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52744883|title=Watford's Adrian Mariappa confirms coronavirus; N'Golo Kante misses training|date=20 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/may/19/premier-league-reveals-six-positive-coronavirus-tests-across-three-clubs|title=Burnley coach Ian Woan among six positive Premier League Covid-19 tests|first=Paul|last=MacInnes|date=19 May 2020|work=The Guardian}}</ref> Later in May, [[Aaron Ramsdale]] of Bournemouth also returned a positive test for the virus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52818258|title=Aaron Ramsdale: Bournemouth 'shook' by positive coronavirus test – Eddie Howe|date=27 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

A number of players, including Manchester City's [[Raheem Sterling]] and [[Sergio Agüero]] and [[Aaron Cresswell]] of West Ham United, voiced concerns relating to the safety of restarting the campaign. [[Danny Rose (footballer, born 1990)|Danny Rose]] of Newcastle United called the decision to restart "a joke".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/manchester-city/story/4093883/man-citys-sterling-ive-had-family-members-die-from-coronavirus|title=Sterling: I've had family members die from virus|date=12 May 2020|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/apr/02/coronavirus-pandemic-aaron-cresswell-petrified-for-his-newborn-baby|title=Coronavirus leaves Aaron Cresswell 'petrified' for his newborn baby|date=2 April 2020|work=The Guardian}}</ref> [[Troy Deeney]] of Watford said he would not return to training because of fear for his family's health.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52721397|title=Troy Deeney: Watford captain says he will not return to training|date=19 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> [[N'Golo Kanté]] of Chelsea also missed training with safety concerns.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/11991873/ngolo-kante-opts-to-miss-chelsea-training-on-wednesday|title=N'Golo Kante opts to miss Chelsea training on Wednesday|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> On 27 May, the clubs voted unanimously to resume [[Contact sport#Limited-contact|contact]] training.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52820291|title=Premier League clubs agree to resume contact training|date=27 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Aston Villa's [[Tyrone Mings]] said the players had not been consulted regarding restarting the league and that the restart was "financially driven".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52866678|title=Tyrone Mings: Premier League players 'last to be consulted' over 'financially driven' restart|date=31 May 2020|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 28 May, clubs agreed that the season would restart on 17 June,<ref>{{Cite news|date=28 May 2020|title=Premier League set to restart on 17 June with Man City v Arsenal and Villa v Sheff Utd|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52833725|access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref> with the two games in hand of Manchester City vs Arsenal and Aston Villa vs Sheffield United,<ref>{{Cite news|title=Premier League fixtures: All 2019/20 remaining games|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11983529/premier-league-fixtures-all-2019-20-remaining-games|website=Sky Sports|access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref> with the first full round of fixtures since March to be played on the weekend of 19–21 June, with all matches played behind closed doors. A plan was announced for all remaining matches to be televised, and to widen the availability of domestic broadcasts: for the first time, the [[BBC]] gained rights to broadcast four live matches on free-to-air television, while Sky announced plans to carry 25 matches on its free-to-air channel [[Pick (TV channel)|Pick]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League to resume on 17th June with Man City v Arsenal|url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/premier-league-return-june-17-man-city-arsenal/|access-date=13 July 2020|website=SportsPro|date=29 May 2020 }}</ref> [[Amazon Prime Video|Amazon]] were allotted four matches and announced it would provide a means of streaming them for free without an [[Amazon Prime]] subscription; on 18 June it was announced that these matches would be carried on its [[video game live streaming]] service [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Amazon's four Premier League matches to be made available free|url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/amazon-prime-premier-league-free-streaming-tv-rights/|access-date=13 July 2020|website=SportsPro|date=3 June 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Amazon's Premier League games to air on Twitch for free|url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/premier-league-amazon-twitch-stream-crowd-noise/|access-date=13 July 2020|website=SportsPro|date=18 June 2020 }}</ref> All broadcasters showed the matches with [[artificial crowd noise]], whilst also providing an alternative option for viewers to watch the matches without the added effects.

On 4 June, the Premier League announced that teams would be allowed to name nine substitutes per match, instead of the usual seven, and that teams could use five substitutes per match instead of three.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52914350| title=Premier League: Five substitutes approved for rest of 2019–20 season| work=[[BBC Sport]]| date=4 June 2020| access-date=4 June 2020}}</ref>

Aston Villa vs. Sheffield United and Manchester City vs. Arsenal on 17 June were the first games played after the pandemic enforced break.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1665216|title=Update on 2019/20 Fantasy Premier League|website=www.premierleague.com |date=30 May 2020 }}</ref>

Financial services company [[Deloitte]] estimated that Premier League clubs would face a £1&nbsp;billion loss of revenue for the 2019–20 season, £500&nbsp;million being accounted for in rebates to broadcasters and loss of matchday revenue.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52999782|title=Coronavirus pandemic set to cost Premier League clubs £1bn in 2019–20 – Deloitte|work=BBC Sport |date=11 June 2020}}</ref>

Further tests for the virus were carried out on 11 and 12 June. Two unnamed people provided a positive result including one player from Norwich City who would be required to [[Isolation (health care)|self-isolate]] thereby missing the first fixture of the restarted season. Following these tests there had been 16 positive results from 8,687 tests.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53036195|title=Norwich player tests positive in latest Premier League coronavirus testing|work=BBC Sport |date=13 June 2020}}</ref>

Before the restart of games the Premier League produced a set of guidelines to be followed at all games. They stipulated that all matches must be played behind closed doors, with the number of key people allowed inside the stadium limited to 300. All stadiums are divided into three zones — red (includes pitch and technical areas), amber (stands) and green (stand concourses) — and there are restrictions on who is allowed to enter each. There is staggered entry on to the pitch for players and staff and no handshakes are allowed before kick-off. Deep cleaning of corner flags, goalposts, substitution boards and match balls takes place before and after each fixture as standard. Extra [[disinfection]], such as of the substitution board after it is used, is likely during matches and at half-time. Additional measures include that players and coaching staff must observe social distancing rules when travelling to and from games, and post-match broadcast interviews must take place pitchside with press conferences conducted virtually.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53009593|title=The Premier League returns – all you need to know|work=BBC Sport |date=16 June 2020}}</ref>

== Teams ==
Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2018–19 EFL Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] and [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. Norwich City and Aston Villa returned to the top flight after absences of three years, while Sheffield United returned after a twelve-year absence. They replaced [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] (both teams relegated to the [[2019–20 EFL Championship|Championship]] after one season back in the top flight) and [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] (relegated after two years in the top flight). Cardiff City's relegation means that this season was the first without a side from [[Wales]] since the [[2010–11 Premier League|2010–11]] season.
